topic: How can beam radius affect root sequence selection and cyclic shift offsets to minimize timing advance estimation errors?
consensus_response: As beam radius increases, preamble duration grows due to larger time uncertainty (δtrt dmax) and delay spread (τmax), reducing sub-carrier interval and increasing sensitivity to CFO. This necessitates cyclic shifts of root ZC sequences to mitigate effects, but excessive utilization leads to high computational complexity in preamble detection. Utilizing a single root ZC sequence with different cyclic shifts can reduce the number of required root sequences and cyclic shift offsets, thus minimizing timing advance estimation errors. Frequency Hopping (FH) can be employed to reduce cyclic shift offset dependent on δtrt dmax, hopping between sub-carriers with different cyclic shifts.
reference_context: The reference context provides insights into preamble design and detection for mobile satellite communication systems, including the effects of beam radius on preamble duration, sub-carrier interval, and sensitivity to CFO. It also discusses the utilization of a single root ZC sequence with different cyclic shifts and Frequency Hopping (FH) as solutions to mitigate these effects.
